source.text: בָּנִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִתְגֹּֽדְד֗וּ וְלֹֽא־תָשִׂ֧ימוּ קָרְחָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין עֵינֵיכֶ֖ם לָמֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Sons [are] you of Yahweh your God; not you will cut yourselves, and not you will make baldness between your eyes for [the] dead.

en.L: You [are] {{gender:children|sons}} of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not cut yourselves, and you shall not make a bald spot between your eyes for the dead.
en.B: You are {{gender:children|sons}} of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not gash yourselves or shave a bald patch on your foreheads in mourning for the dead.
en.R: You are the {{gender:children|sons}} of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. So when someone dies, do not cut your bodies or shave the front of your heads to show your sorrow.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} [{{plural_you:son|sois}}] hijos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}. No {{plural_you:se harán|os haréis}} cortes, ni {{plural_you:se raparán|os raparéis}} entre los ojos por un muerto.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} hijos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}. No {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} heridas ni {{plural_you:se rapen|os rapéis}} la frente en señal de luto por un muerto.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} los hijos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}. Por eso, cuando alguien muera, no {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} cortes en el cuerpo ni {{plural_you:se rapen|os rapéis}} la parte delantera de la cabeza para mostrar {{plural_you:su tristeza|vuestra tristeza}}.

fr.L: Vous [êtes] des {{gender:enfants|fils}} {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu. Vous ne vous ferez pas d’incisions, et vous ne vous raserez pas [la tête] entre les yeux pour un mort.
fr.B: Vous êtes des {{gender:enfants|fils}} {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu. Ne vous tailladez pas le corps et ne vous rasez pas le front pour porter le deuil d’un mort.
fr.R: Vous êtes les {{gender:enfants|fils}} {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu. Alors, quand quelqu’un meurt, ne vous faites pas de coupures sur le corps et ne vous rasez pas le devant de la tête pour montrer votre tristesse.

sw.L: Ninyi [ni] wana wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu. Hamtajikatakata, wala hamtajinyoa upara kati ya macho yenu kwa ajili ya mfu.
sw.B: Ninyi ni wana wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu. Msijichanje, wala msinyoe upara kwenye paji la uso mkiomboleza kwa ajili ya aliyekufa.
sw.R: Ninyi ni watoto wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu. Kwa hiyo mtu akifa, msijikate miilini mwenu wala msinyoe nywele za mbele ya kichwa ili kuonyesha huzuni yenu.

vi.L: Các ngươi [là] {{gender:con cái|con trai}} của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi. Các ngươi không được tự rạch mình, và không được cạo trọc giữa hai mắt các ngươi vì người chết.
vi.B: Anh em là {{gender:con cái|con trai}} của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em. Đừng rạch mình hay cạo trọc phía trên trán để than khóc người chết.
vi.R: Anh em là {{gender:con cái|con trai}} của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em. Vậy khi có người qua đời, đừng rạch thân thể mình hay cạo trọc phần tóc phía trước đầu để tỏ lòng thương tiếc.

ko.L: 너희는 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 자녀이다. 너희는 죽은 사람 때문에 너희 몸을 베지 말고, 너희 눈 사이를 밀어 대머리가 되게 하지 말아라.
ko.B: 너희는 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 자녀이다. 죽은 사람을 애도한다고 몸에 상처를 내거나 이마 위의 머리를 밀지 말아라.
ko.R: 여러분은 여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 자녀입니다. 그러니 누가 죽었을 때 슬픔을 나타내려고 몸에 상처를 내거나 앞머리를 밀지 마십시오.

pt.L: Vocês [são] filhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês. Não se cortarão, e não farão uma parte calva entre os olhos de vocês por um morto.
pt.B: Vocês são filhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês. Não farão cortes no corpo nem rasparão a frente da cabeça em luto por um morto.
pt.R: Vocês são os filhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de vocês. Por isso, quando alguém morrer, não cortem o corpo nem raspem a frente da cabeça para mostrar a sua tristeza.

am.L: እናንተ የአምላካችሁ {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ልጆች [ናችሁ]፤ ሰውነታችሁን አትቁረጡ፤ ለሞተም ሰው በዓይኖቻችሁ መካከል ጠጉራችሁን አትላጩ።
am.B: እናንተ የአምላካችሁ {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ልጆች ናችሁ። ለሞተ ሰው በማዘን ሰውነታችሁን አትቆራርጡ፤ ግንባራችሁንም አትላጩ።
am.R: እናንተ የአምላካችሁ {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} ልጆች ናችሁ። ስለዚህ ሰው ሲሞት ሐዘናችሁን ለማሳየት ሰውነታችሁን አትቁረጡ፤ የራስ ጠጉራችሁንም ከፊት በኩል አትላጩ።

decisions.choice: children of the LORD your God: Israel belongs to God as a family belongs to its father
decisions.reason: The word is "sons", but it is said of the whole people, men and women. God called Israel his firstborn son (Exodus 4:22), and Moses has said that the LORD trains Israel as a father trains his son (8:5; compare 1:31; 32:5-6; Hosea 11:1). Moses is still speaking in the speech that began at 5:1. Because the people belong to God in this way, they must not take up the mourning customs of the peoples around them; verse 2 gives the reason in full.

decisions.choice: cut yourselves, make a bald spot for the dead: rites of mourning practiced by Israel's neighbors
decisions.reason: Gashing the body and shaving part of the head were known signs of grief in the ancient world (Isaiah 15:2; Jeremiah 16:6; 41:5; 47:5), and the prophets of Baal cut themselves in worship (1 Kings 18:28). Leviticus forbids the same rites to all Israel and to the priests (Leviticus 19:27-28; 21:5). The law does not forbid grief; it forbids marking the body in the way the nations did.

decisions.choice: between your eyes: on the forehead, the front of the head above the eyes
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used for the place where the words of God are to be worn as a sign (6:8; 11:18). Here it names the front of the scalp, which was shaved bare in mourning.

decisions.choice: on your foreheads; in mourning for the dead / when someone dies ... to show your sorrow
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where "between your eyes" is and that these rites were signs of grief, as Leviticus 19:28 does. Literal keeps "between your eyes for the dead".

decisions.choice: "hijos" with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change; French has "enfants|fils" as the English has "children|sons".

decisions.choice: {{gender:con cái|con trai}} for Israel as the LORD's sons
decisions.reason: The same two wordings as for "your sons" (11:2): "con cái" by default, "con trai" as the traditional alternative.

decisions.choice: filhos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English puts "sons" under the gender setting because it is said of the whole people (m1). Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters, so there is no second wording to offer, as with "os filhos de Israel" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md). Readable says "para mostrar a sua tristeza", the wording of Leviticus 19:28 for the same rite.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of this chapter
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change; the pronouns for God are the ordinary ones ("እርሱ", "የራሱ").

decisions.choice: No gender span on "ልጆች" (children)
decisions.reason: "ልጆች" already includes daughters (the terms list), so the English span has nothing to change.

records.literal_gloss: For a people holy [are] you to Yahweh your God, and you has chosen Yahweh to be for him for a people of treasured possession out of all the peoples which [are] on [the] face of the ground.

en.L: For you [are] a holy people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to be a people of special possession for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of all the peoples that [are] on the face of the ground.
en.B: For you are a people set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own special treasure.
en.R: You belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God as a holy people. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose you out of all the nations on earth to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own special treasure.

es.L: Porque pueblo santo [eres] tú para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, y a ti te ha escogido {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} para que seas para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} un pueblo de posesión preciada entre todos los pueblos que [están] sobre la faz de la tierra.
es.B: Porque tú eres un pueblo consagrado como santo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios. De entre todos los pueblos que hay sobre la faz de la tierra, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha escogido para que seas {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} tesoro personal.
es.R: Tú perteneces {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios como pueblo santo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te escogió de entre todas las naciones de la tierra para que seas {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} tesoro especial.

fr.L: Car tu [es] un peuple saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a choisi pour être pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un peuple, un trésor particulier, parmi tous les peuples qui [sont] sur la face du sol.
fr.B: Car tu es un peuple mis à part, saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Parmi tous les peuples qui sont sur la face de la terre, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a choisi pour être {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre trésor.
fr.R: Tu appartiens {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ton Dieu comme un peuple saint. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a choisi parmi toutes les nations de la terre pour être {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trésor à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana wewe [ni] taifa takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekuchagua uwe {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} taifa la milki ya pekee kutoka katika mataifa yote yaliyo juu ya uso wa ardhi.
sw.B: Kwa maana wewe ni taifa lililotengwa kuwa takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Kati ya mataifa yote yaliyo juu ya uso wa dunia, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekuchagua uwe hazina {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya pekee.
sw.R: Wewe ni mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, taifa takatifu. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuchagua kati ya mataifa yote duniani uwe hazina {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya pekee.

vi.L: Vì ngươi [là] một dân thánh cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chọn ngươi để làm một dân, báu vật riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, giữa mọi dân tộc ở trên mặt đất.
vi.B: Vì anh em là một dân được biệt riêng ra thánh cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em. Từ giữa mọi dân tộc trên mặt đất, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chọn anh em làm báu vật riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Anh em thuộc về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, là một dân thánh. Trong mọi dân tộc trên đất, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chọn anh em làm báu vật riêng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 너는 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩한 백성이기 때문이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 땅 위에 있는 모든 백성 가운데서 너를 택하셔서 그분께 특별한 소유의 백성이 되게 하셨다.
ko.B: 너희는 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 거룩하게 구별된 백성이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 땅 위의 모든 민족 가운데서 너희를 택하셔서 그분의 소중한 보물로 삼으셨다.
ko.R: 여러분은 여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 속한 거룩한 백성입니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 세상의 모든 민족 가운데서 여러분을 택하셔서 그분의 특별한 보물로 삼으셨습니다.

pt.L: Porque tu [és] um povo santo {{divine_name:para o SENHOR|para Javé}}, o teu Deus, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} te escolheu para seres um povo de propriedade especial para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, dentre todos os povos que [há] sobre a face da terra.
pt.B: Porque tu és um povo separado como santo {{divine_name:para o SENHOR|para Javé}}, o teu Deus. Dentre todos os povos que há sobre a face da terra, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} te escolheu para seres o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} tesouro especial.
pt.R: Tu pertences {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o teu Deus, como um povo santo. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} te escolheu dentre todas as nações da terra para seres o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} tesouro especial.

am.L: ለአምላክህ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} የተቀደስህ ሕዝብ ነህና፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በምድር ፊት ላይ ካሉት ሕዝቦች ሁሉ ለእርሱ የግል ሀብት የሆነ ሕዝብ ትሆን ዘንድ መርጦሃል።
am.B: ለአምላክህ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} የተለየህ ቅዱስ ሕዝብ ነህና። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በምድር ገጽ ላይ ካሉት ሕዝቦች ሁሉ መካከል የራሱ ውድ ሀብት እንድትሆን መርጦሃል።
am.R: አንተ ለአምላክህ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} የተለየህ ቅዱስ ሕዝብ ነህ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} በምድር ላይ ካሉት ሕዝቦች ሁሉ መካከል የራሱ ውድ ሀብት እንድትሆን መረጠህ።

decisions.choice: for: the reason for verse 1, and the ground of the food laws that follow
decisions.reason: Israel must not mourn as the nations do because it is a holy people. The same words return in verse 21 to close the food laws, so this sentence stands over the whole section: what Israel does with its body and what it eats both show whose people it is.

decisions.choice: a holy people: a people set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: To be holy is to be set apart for God and so marked off from what is common or unclean (Exodus 19:6; Leviticus 11:44-45). Here it is not a reward for good conduct but a fact God has made true by choosing Israel; the commands that follow show how Israel is to live as what it already is (7:6; 26:19).

decisions.choice: a people of special possession: a personal treasure, prized and owned
decisions.reason: The word is used of a king's own store of treasure (1 Chronicles 29:2-3; Ecclesiastes 2:8). God uses it of Israel in Exodus 19:5 and Deuteronomy 7:6 and 26:18, and 1 Peter 2:9 takes it up. The verse is almost word for word the same as 7:6.

decisions.choice: you (singular): the people addressed as one
decisions.reason: Verse 1 speaks to the people with plural verbs; here the address turns singular, as Deuteronomy often does, because Israel is one people before God. The meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: own special treasure
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 19:5, Balanced and Readable say "own special treasure" to bring out both ownership and value; Literal has "special possession".

decisions.choice: tu (Hebrew singular), vocês (Hebrew plural): word by word at Literal, sentence by sentence at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As 4:1 and 6:1 set it for the whole book. Moses speaks to Israel now in the plural (verse 1) and now in the singular, as one people (m4). Literal follows the Hebrew number word by word, "tu" or "vocês". Balanced and Readable follow it sentence by sentence, so that no sentence mixes "tu" and "vocês", as Leviticus 19:2 does. With "tu" the formula is "{{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o teu Deus"; with "vocês", "o Deus de vocês".

decisions.choice: um povo de propriedade especial (L); o seu tesouro especial (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Exodus 19:5 words the same term (m3): "propriedade especial" at Literal, "tesouro especial" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "የግል ሀብት" (L), "ውድ ሀብት" (B, R) for "a people of special possession"
decisions.reason: The settled choice for segullah (Exodus 19:5).

decisions.choice: abomination: something the LORD detests and will not accept
decisions.reason: This is the word used for the gods and worship of the nations (7:25-26; 12:31), for dishonest weights (25:16) and for certain acts in Leviticus 18:22. Leviticus 11 uses a different word, "detestable", for forbidden creatures. Here the stronger word sums up all the foods forbidden in verses 4-21: to eat them would be to take into oneself what God rejects.

decisions.choice: deer and gazelle: wild animals hunted for food
decisions.reason: The deer and the gazelle were the best-known game animals, hunted and eaten but not offered in sacrifice (12:15, 22; 15:22; 1 Kings 5:3). Their presence in this list shows that the clean animals include wild ones as well as livestock.

decisions.choice: roe deer, wild goat, ibex, antelope, mountain sheep: probable identifications
decisions.reason: Several of these names occur only here or very rarely, so they are identified from related words and ancient translations. The third may be a kind of deer (1 Kings 5:3). The fourth is probably a wild goat, and the fifth a mountain goat such as the ibex. The sixth is an animal caught in nets (Isaiah 51:20), perhaps an antelope or a wild ox. The seventh is probably a wild sheep. All are animals with split hooves that chew the cud, as verse 6 requires.

en.L: Nevertheless, these you shall not eat, of those that bring up the cud or of those that divide the hoof [and are] cloven: the camel, and the hare, and the rock badger, for they bring up the cud, but the hoof they do not divide; they [are] unclean to you.
en.B: Yet you must not eat these, even though they chew the cud or have split hooves: the camel, the hare and the rock badger. They chew the cud but do not have split hooves, so they are unclean for you.
en.R: But do not eat the animals that have only one of the two signs. The camel, the hare and the rock badger chew the cud, but their hooves are not split. So they are unclean for you.

es.L: Pero de estos no {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}, de los que rumian y de los que dividen la pezuña hendida: el camello, y la liebre, y el damán, porque rumian, pero no dividen la pezuña; impuros [son] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Sin embargo, no {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} estos, aunque rumien o tengan la pezuña partida: el camello, la liebre y el damán. Rumian, pero no tienen la pezuña partida; por eso son impuros para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:coman|comáis}} los animales que solo tienen una de las dos señales. El camello, la liebre y el damán rumian, pero sus pezuñas no están partidas. Por eso son impuros para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Toutefois, voici ceux que vous ne mangerez pas, parmi ceux qui ruminent et parmi ceux qui ont le sabot divisé [et] fendu : le chameau, et le lièvre, et le daman, car ils ruminent, mais ils n’ont pas le sabot divisé ; ils [sont] impurs pour vous.
fr.B: Mais vous ne mangerez pas ceux-ci, même s’ils ruminent ou ont le sabot fendu : le chameau, le lièvre et le daman. Ils ruminent, mais n’ont pas le sabot fendu ; ils sont donc impurs pour vous.
fr.R: Mais ne mangez pas les animaux qui n’ont qu’un seul des deux signes. Le chameau, le lièvre et le daman ruminent, mais leurs sabots ne sont pas fendus. Ils sont donc impurs pour vous.

sw.L: Lakini hawa hamtawala, kati ya wale wanaocheua na kati ya wale wenye kwato zilizogawanyika [na] kupasuka: ngamia, na sungura, na pimbi, kwa maana wao wanacheua, lakini kwato zao hazikugawanyika; wao [ni] najisi kwenu.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, msiwale hawa, ingawa wanacheua au wana kwato zilizopasuka: ngamia, sungura na pimbi. Wanacheua, lakini hawana kwato zilizopasuka; kwa hiyo ni najisi kwenu.
sw.R: Lakini msiwale wanyama wenye alama moja tu kati ya hizo mbili. Ngamia, sungura na pimbi wanacheua, lakini kwato zao hazijapasuka. Kwa hiyo ni najisi kwenu.

vi.L: Tuy nhiên, những con này các ngươi không được ăn, trong những con nhai lại hoặc những con có móng rẽ chẻ khe: con lạc đà, con thỏ rừng và con đa-man, vì chúng nhai lại nhưng móng không rẽ; chúng ô uế cho các ngươi.
vi.B: Nhưng anh em không được ăn những con sau đây, dù chúng nhai lại hay có móng chẻ: con lạc đà, con thỏ rừng và con đa-man. Chúng nhai lại nhưng móng không chẻ, nên chúng ô uế đối với anh em.
vi.R: Nhưng đừng ăn những con thú chỉ có một trong hai dấu hiệu ấy. Con lạc đà, con thỏ rừng và con đa-man nhai lại, nhưng móng chúng không chẻ. Vì vậy chúng ô uế đối với anh em.

ko.L: 그러나 되새김질하는 것들 가운데서나 굽이 갈라지고 쪼개진 것들 가운데서 이것들은 너희가 먹지 말아라. 낙타와 산토끼와 바위너구리이다. 그것들은 되새김질은 하지만 굽이 갈라지지 않았으니, 그것들은 너희에게 부정하다.
ko.B: 그러나 되새김질을 하거나 굽이 갈라졌더라도 다음 짐승들은 먹지 말아라. 낙타와 산토끼와 바위너구리이다. 그것들은 되새김질은 하지만 굽이 갈라지지 않았으므로 너희에게 부정한 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 이 두 가지 가운데 한 가지만 있는 짐승은 먹으면 안 됩니다. 낙타와 산토끼와 바위너구리는 되새김질은 하지만 굽이 갈라지지 않았습니다. 그러므로 그것들은 여러분에게 부정합니다.

pt.L: Contudo, estes vocês não comerão, dentre os que ruminam e dentre os que dividem o casco fendido: o camelo, e a lebre, e o hírax, porque eles ruminam, mas o casco não dividem; eles [são] impuros para vocês.
pt.B: Mas vocês não comerão estes, ainda que ruminem ou tenham o casco dividido: o camelo, a lebre e o hírax. Eles ruminam, mas não têm o casco dividido; por isso são impuros para vocês.
pt.R: Mas não comam os animais que têm só um desses dois sinais. O camelo, a lebre e o hírax, um pequeno animal que vive entre as rochas, ruminam, mas não têm o casco dividido. Por isso eles são impuros para vocês.

am.L: ነገር ግን ከሚያመነዥኩትና ሰኮናቸው ከተሰነጠቀው እነዚህን አትበሉም፤ ግመልን፣ ጥንቸልንና ሽኮኮን፤ ያመነዥካሉና፤ ሰኮናቸው ግን አልተሰነጠቀም፤ ለእናንተ ርኩሳን ናቸው።
am.B: ነገር ግን ቢያመነዥኩም ወይም ሰኮናቸው የተሰነጠቀ ቢሆንም እነዚህን አትብሉ፤ ግመል፣ ጥንቸልና ሽኮኮ። ያመነዥካሉ፤ ሰኮናቸው ግን የተሰነጠቀ አይደለም፤ ስለዚህ ለእናንተ ርኩሳን ናቸው።
am.R: ከሁለቱ ምልክቶች አንዱ ብቻ ያላቸውን እንስሳት ግን አትብሉ። ግመል፣ ጥንቸልና ሽኮኮ ያመነዥካሉ፤ ሰኮናቸው ግን አልተሰነጠቀም። ስለዚህ ለእናንተ ርኩሳን ናቸው።

decisions.choice: unclean: ritually impure, forbidden as food to Israel
decisions.reason: Unclean is not the same as dirty or sinful. It is a state that God's law assigns to certain animals, bodies and objects, and its opposite is clean (Leviticus 10:10; 11:4, 47). These animals are unclean "to you": forbidden to Israel as food. Living camels could still be ridden and handled. See Leviticus 11:4.

decisions.choice: rock badger: probably the rock hyrax, a small animal that lives among rocks
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:5. The animal lives among the rocks (Psalm 104:18; Proverbs 30:26), which fits the rock hyrax, a small furry animal about the size of a rabbit. It is not a true badger. The identification is widely accepted, though not certain.

decisions.choice: the camel, the hare and the rock badger: each has only one of the two signs
decisions.reason: A camel's foot has two toes resting on a broad, soft pad, not two separate hard hooves. The hare and the hyrax do not have the several stomachs of cattle and sheep, but they move their jaws constantly as if chewing; the law describes them as an observer sees them (Leviticus 11:4-6). Deuteronomy names the hare before the rock badger; Leviticus has the reverse order.

decisions.choice: unclean for you
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 11:4, "to you" means as far as you are concerned, for your eating, and Balanced and Readable say "for you".

decisions.choice: o hírax; R adds "um pequeno animal que vive entre as rochas"
decisions.reason: As Leviticus 11:5: the rock hyrax (m2) has no traditional Portuguese name that readers know, so all levels use its name, "hírax", and Readable says what it is.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַ֠חֲזִיר כִּֽי־מַפְרִ֨יס פַּרְסָ֥ה הוּא֙ וְלֹ֣א גֵרָ֔ה טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶ֑ם מִבְּשָׂרָם֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ וּבְנִבְלָתָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִגָּֽעוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the pig, for dividing [a] hoof [is] it, and not cud; unclean [is] it to you; from their meat not you will eat, and their carcass not you will touch.

en.L: And the pig, for it divides the hoof, but [chews] no cud; it [is] unclean to you. Of their meat you shall not eat, and their carcass you shall not touch.
en.B: The pig has split hooves but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you. Do not eat any of their meat, and do not touch them when they are dead.
en.R: The pig has split hooves, but it does not chew the cud. So it is unclean for you. Do not eat the meat of any of these animals. Do not touch their bodies after they have died.

es.L: Y el cerdo, porque divide la pezuña, pero no [rumia]; impuro [es] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. De su carne no {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}, y sus cadáveres no {{plural_you:tocarán|tocaréis}}.
es.B: El cerdo tiene la pezuña partida, pero no rumia; es impuro para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. No {{plural_you:coman|comáis}} nada de su carne ni {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} sus cuerpos cuando estén muertos.
es.R: El cerdo tiene las pezuñas partidas, pero no rumia. Por eso es impuro para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. No {{plural_you:coman|comáis}} la carne de ninguno de estos animales. No {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} sus cuerpos después de que hayan muerto.

fr.L: Et le porc, car il a le sabot divisé, mais [ne rumine] pas ; il [est] impur pour vous. Vous ne mangerez pas de leur chair, et vous ne toucherez pas leur cadavre.
fr.B: Le porc a le sabot fendu, mais il ne rumine pas ; il est impur pour vous. Ne mangez rien de leur viande et ne les touchez pas quand ils sont morts.
fr.R: Le porc a des sabots fendus, mais il ne rumine pas. Il est donc impur pour vous. Ne mangez pas la viande de ces animaux. Ne touchez pas leur corps après leur mort.

sw.L: Na nguruwe, kwa maana yeye ana kwato iliyogawanyika, lakini [hacheui]; yeye [ni] najisi kwenu. Nyama yao hamtakula, na mizoga yao hamtaigusa.
sw.B: Nguruwe ana kwato zilizopasuka, lakini hacheui; ni najisi kwenu. Msile nyama yao yoyote, wala msiwaguse wakiwa wamekufa.
sw.R: Nguruwe ana kwato zilizopasuka, lakini hacheui. Kwa hiyo ni najisi kwenu. Msile nyama ya yeyote kati ya wanyama hao. Msiiguse miili yao baada ya kufa.

vi.L: Còn con heo, vì nó có móng rẽ nhưng không nhai lại; nó ô uế cho các ngươi. Các ngươi không được ăn thịt chúng, và không được chạm vào xác chúng.
vi.B: Con heo có móng chẻ nhưng không nhai lại; nó ô uế đối với anh em. Không được ăn thịt các con vật ấy, cũng không được chạm vào xác chúng.
vi.R: Con heo có móng chẻ nhưng không nhai lại. Vì vậy nó ô uế đối với anh em. Đừng ăn thịt những con vật này. Đừng chạm vào xác chúng khi chúng đã chết.

ko.L: 그리고 돼지는 굽이 갈라졌으나 되새김질은 하지 않으니, 그것은 너희에게 부정하다. 너희는 그것들의 고기를 먹지 말고, 그것들의 주검을 만지지 말아라.
ko.B: 돼지는 굽이 갈라졌지만 되새김질은 하지 않으므로 너희에게 부정한 것이다. 이런 짐승들의 고기는 먹지 말고, 죽은 것은 만지지도 말아라.
ko.R: 돼지는 굽이 갈라졌지만 되새김질을 하지 않습니다. 그러므로 여러분에게 부정합니다. 이런 짐승들의 고기는 먹으면 안 됩니다. 그것들이 죽은 뒤에 그 몸을 만져도 안 됩니다.

pt.L: E o porco, porque ele divide o casco, mas não [rumina]; ele [é] impuro para vocês. Da carne deles vocês não comerão, e na carcaça deles não tocarão.
pt.B: O porco tem o casco dividido, mas não rumina; ele é impuro para vocês. Não comerão nada da carne deles e não tocarão neles quando estiverem mortos.
pt.R: O porco tem o casco dividido, mas não rumina. Por isso ele é impuro para vocês. Não comam a carne de nenhum desses animais. Não toquem no corpo deles depois que morrerem.

am.L: አሳማም ሰኮናው የተሰነጠቀ ነውና፤ ነገር ግን አያመነዥክም፤ ለእናንተ ርኩስ ነው። ከሥጋቸው አትበሉም፤ በድናቸውንም አትነኩም።
am.B: አሳማ ሰኮናው የተሰነጠቀ ነው፤ ነገር ግን አያመነዥክም፤ ለእናንተ ርኩስ ነው። ከሥጋቸው ምንም አትብሉ፤ ሞተው ሳሉም አትንኳቸው።
am.R: አሳማ የተሰነጠቀ ሰኮና አለው፤ ነገር ግን አያመነዥክም። ስለዚህ ለእናንተ ርኩስ ነው። ከእነዚህ እንስሳት የአንዱንም ሥጋ አትብሉ። ከሞቱም በኋላ አካላቸውን አትንኩ።

decisions.choice: the pig: an animal with split hooves that does not chew the cud
decisions.reason: The pig is named with the opposite lack to the camel, hare and rock badger (Leviticus 11:7). Later Scripture treats eating pork as a mark of turning away from God (Isaiah 65:4; 66:17).

decisions.choice: and not cud: it does not chew the cud
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short here, "and not cud", with no verb. Leviticus 11:7 gives the full phrase, "it does not chew the cud", and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: their meat ... their carcass: of all four animals of verses 7-8, when dead
decisions.reason: "Their" covers the camel, the hare, the rock badger and the pig. The carcass is the body of an animal that has died or been killed; touching it made a person unclean (Leviticus 11:8, 24-28). The ban concerns these animals when dead, not the living camel.

decisions.choice: when they are dead / of any of these animals ... after they have died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "when they are dead" for "their carcass", as in Leviticus 11:8, and Readable makes clear that "their" means all the animals just named.

source.text: אֶת־זֶה֙ תֹּֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמָּ֑יִם כֹּ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: This you will eat from all which [is] in the waters: all which [belongs] to it fin and scale you will eat.

en.L: This you may eat of all that [is] in the waters: everything that has fin and scale you may eat.
en.B: Among the creatures of the water, any that have fins and scales are yours to eat.
en.R: You may eat water animals that have fins and scales.

es.L: Esto {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} de todo lo que [está] en las aguas: todo lo que tiene aletas y escamas lo {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}.
es.B: De entre los animales del agua, {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} comer todos los que tienen aletas y escamas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} comer los animales del agua que tienen aletas y escamas.

fr.L: Voici ce que vous mangerez de tout ce qui [est] dans les eaux : tout ce qui a nageoire et écaille, vous le mangerez.
fr.B: Parmi les créatures des eaux, vous pourrez manger toutes celles qui ont des nageoires et des écailles.
fr.R: Vous pouvez manger les animaux d’eau qui ont des nageoires et des écailles.

sw.L: Hiki mtakula katika vyote vilivyo majini: kila kilicho na mapezi na magamba mtakula.
sw.B: Kati ya viumbe vya majini, mnaweza kula vyote vyenye mapezi na magamba.
sw.R: Mnaweza kula wanyama wa majini walio na mapezi na magamba.

vi.L: Đây [là những con] các ngươi được ăn trong mọi loài ở dưới nước: mọi con có vây và vảy, các ngươi được ăn.
vi.B: Trong các loài sống dưới nước, anh em được ăn những con có vây và vảy.
vi.R: Anh em được ăn những con vật dưới nước có vây và có vảy.

ko.L: 물속에 있는 모든 것 가운데서 너희가 먹을 수 있는 것은 이러하다. 지느러미와 비늘이 있는 것은 모두 너희가 먹을 수 있다.
ko.B: 물에 사는 것 가운데서 지느러미와 비늘이 있는 것은 무엇이든 먹어도 된다.
ko.R: 물에 사는 동물 가운데서 지느러미와 비늘이 있는 것은 먹어도 됩니다.

pt.L: Isto vocês podem comer de tudo o que [há] nas águas: tudo o que tem barbatana e escama vocês podem comer.
pt.B: Dos animais que vivem na água, vocês podem comer todos os que têm barbatanas e escamas.
pt.R: Vocês podem comer os animais da água que têm barbatanas e escamas.

am.L: በውኃ ውስጥ ካሉት ሁሉ ይህን ትበላላችሁ፤ ክንፍና ቅርፊት ያለውን ሁሉ ትበላላችሁ።
am.B: በውኃ ውስጥ ከሚኖሩት ፍጥረታት ክንፍና ቅርፊት ያላቸውን ሁሉ መብላት ትችላላችሁ።
am.R: በውኃ ውስጥ ከሚኖሩት ክንፍና ቅርፊት ያላቸውን መብላት ትችላላችሁ።

decisions.choice: fin and scale: the two marks of water creatures that may be eaten
decisions.reason: As with land animals, a water creature must have both marks. Most fish have both; eels, catfish, shellfish and other sea creatures do not. Leviticus 11:9-12 gives the same rule at more length.

source.text: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵֽין־ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And all which there [is] not to it fin and scale not you will eat; unclean [is] it to you.

en.L: And all that does not have fin and scale you shall not eat; it [is] unclean to you.

en.L: You shall not eat any carcass. To the sojourner who [is] within your gates you may give it, and he may eat it, or [you may] sell [it] to a foreigner; for you [are] a holy people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
en.B: Do not eat anything that has died on its own. The outsider living in your towns may have it to eat if you give it to them, or a foreigner may buy it from you. For you are a people set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
en.R: Do not eat any animal that has died by itself. You may give it to an outsider who lives in your town, and they may eat it. Or you may sell it to someone from another country. This is because you belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God as a holy people. Do not cook a young goat in milk from its own mother.
